title: Stop payment vs insufficient funds - does it change the case
p1: A cheque bounces, but the reason behind it can completely change how people view the situation. Many assume that a stop payment and insufficient funds are treated as two totally different legal problems.
p2: The surprising part is that the result is often not decided only by the reason written by the bank. A stop payment instruction does not automatically erase responsibility. If the cheque was issued towards a genuine liability and other legal conditions are met, the case may still continue. Similarly, insufficient funds is a common reason for dishonour, but it is not the only factor considered.
p3: The real question is why the cheque was issued, whether a valid debt existed, and whether required legal steps were followed after dishonour. The bank's return reason is just one piece of the puzzle. A practical takeaway: never assume a stop payment notice is a guaranteed defence or that every bounced cheque creates the same outcome.
conclusion: Have you ever seen a cheque dispute where the reason for dishonour changed the way people understood the case?
